question: Why is cefuroxime short, and what do we do?

steps.title: Our stock in three hospitals
steps.purpose: Read on-hand stock and 28-day use where each hospital keeps it.
steps.finding: 2 stock lines across 2 hospitals, 1 presentation, in units of use.

steps.title: Where our supply is made
steps.purpose: Follow each product's label to the plants it names, and place each plant in FDA's registration file.
steps.finding: 1 plant links on 1 labels; 1 placed in FDA's registration file.

steps.purpose: Read Corvale General's approved interchanges for these items.

steps.title: Which links can't be trusted
steps.purpose: Run the semantic layer's key rules (NDC and unit of use) over each hospital's stock, and name the rows they reject.
steps.finding: 11 stock rows across the system fail the NDC rule; 0 of them are this drug. Every row is in a shared unit of use.

explanation.headline: Cefuroxime is not on FDA's shortage list as of 2026-10-21; the label for Hikma's product names a plant in Portugal with a history of VAI and OAI inspections

sentences.text: FDA's drug shortage list does not include cefuroxime as of 2026-10-21.
The product label for Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. (NDC 00143997722) identifies the manufacturing plant as HIKMA FARMACEUTICA (PORTUGAL), S.A. (FEI 3002807173) in Portugal.
FDA inspection records for that plant show a VAI classification in 2011, an OAI classification in 2014, and subsequent VAI classifications in 2015, 2016, 2020, and 2023.
A Warning Letter was issued to the plant on 2014-10-21.
Corvale East holds 158 vials of the 1.5 g presentation with 10.5 days on hand; Corvale General holds 367 vials with 25.6 days on hand.
The rule‑based best option is to buy from B. Braun Medical Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today and whose label names no plant we could place.

memory.text: Decision on lidocaine: switch lidocaine 1% 30 mL vials to 5 mL vials in the ED to reduce waste during the shortage. Rationale: Single-dose waste was a third of use (demo history). Approved by Alex Morgan, PharmD.

Decision on cisplatin: transfer cisplatin between Corvale hospitals weekly instead of buying grey-market stock. Rationale: Grey-market offers were 6 to 10 times contract price with unverifiable pedigree (demo history). Approved by Jordan Hale, PharmD.
